segments.flavor: the station ID sweeper, landing on the tagline
segments.text:
Adam: [cheerful] Arcade. Two buttons, one stick, and the whole afternoon gone.
Adam: Insert coin. Here comes the music.

segments.flavor: the station ID sweeper, a secret-wall gag
segments.text:
Adam: This is Arcade, where every hallway has a secret.
Nicole: Push against the wall for four seconds. Trust me.
Adam: Ohhh that's optimal. Play the track.

segments.flavor: the station ID sweeper, the high score promise
segments.text:
Adam: Arcade. Your high score is safe with us. Mostly.
Adam: Hands on the controller, the song is starting.

segments.flavor: the station ID sweeper, the hummed soundtrack
segments.text:
Adam: Arcade. The soundtrack you hummed long after the console stopped working.
Adam: Still humming it. Volume up, here it comes.

segments.flavor: a real-life situation described entirely in game mechanics, landing a genuine punchline
segments.text:
Adam: Parallel parking is a precision platforming section. The curb has a hitbox, and it is generous.
Adam: One attempt, no scratches, no retries. Ohhh that's optimal. Somebody roll the music.

segments.flavor: a real-life situation described entirely in game mechanics, landing a genuine punchline
segments.text:
Adam: Making coffee before your eyes open is playing with stick drift. You will overshoot the mug.
Adam: Recalibrate, wipe the counter, accept the damage. Next track is already loading.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} like a high score entry; Adam rates the run
segments.text:
Adam: That set goes on the board under three letters. A-D-M. Do not challenge it.
Adam: A clean run, zero continues, and style points for that ending. More music, right now.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} like a high score entry; Adam rates the run
segments.text:
Adam: The last two tracks landed back to back with no gap. Frame perfect segue.
Adam: I am giving that an S rank and the board agrees. Keep it rolling.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} like a high score entry; Adam rates the run
segments.text:
Adam: New entry on the board for that last stretch of music. Gold split, no deaths, and no menu time.
Adam: Initials are in and my hands are off the stick. The next runner needs a soundtrack.

segments.flavor: Nicole's lore corner: an absurd 'fact' declared canon with total confidence
segments.text:
Nicole: Lore corner. Every shopping cart has one bad wheel because the cart is cursed loot.
Adam: Cursed loot. So the wobble is a stat penalty?
Nicole: Minus two to steering, plus one to humility. It is canon now.
Adam: Ha! Sold. Push the cart, play the song.

segments.flavor: Nicole's lore corner: an absurd 'fact' declared canon with total confidence
segments.text:
Adam: Nicole has the lore face. Give us the fact.
Nicole: The last slice in any box is behind an invisible wall. Nobody may take it.
Adam: Ohhh that explains so much. It sits there glowing until someone is brave.
Nicole: Canon. Dust it off later. Track, please.

segments.flavor: Emma reports from inside a game as an NPC with feelings about the player's behavior
segments.text:
Adam: Emma is reporting from inside a shop menu. Emma, status?
Emma: The player has opened my shop forty times and bought nothing.
Nicole: Forty.
Emma: I have said welcome forty times. My voice is a loop and I am tired.
Adam: Hang in there, Emma. Music will help.

segments.flavor: a real-life situation described entirely in game mechanics, landing a genuine punchline
segments.text:
Adam: Building flat-pack furniture is a co-op puzzle with no tutorial and one shared inventory.
Nicole: And one player is holding the manual upside down.
Adam: Then the screw. There is always one screw left over.
Nicole: That is the collectible. You missed a room.
Adam: Pshhh. I am not rebuilding the shelf for a trophy.
Nicole: Completionists would. Let the music carry us past it.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} like a high score entry; Adam rates the run
segments.text:
Adam: Putting that last track on the board. Three letters, all caps, fists up.
Nicole: You always enter the same three letters.
Adam: Consistency is a speedrun virtue. I rate that run an A minus.
Nicole: Minus for what?
Adam: The fade at the end cost me two frames. Two.
Nicole: You are unwell, and I mean that warmly. Play the next one.

segments.flavor: Nicole's lore corner: an absurd 'fact' declared canon with total confidence
segments.text:
Adam: Lore corner. Nicole, hit us.
Nicole: The smell before rain is the world loading the outdoor texture pack.
Adam: Oh. OH. That is why it smells like nothing indoors.
Nicole: Indoors is a smaller map. Cheaper to render, fewer smells.
Adam: Is this canon or is this you talking?
Nicole: Both. It is canon because I said it. Roll the tune.

segments.flavor: Emma reports from inside a game as an NPC with feelings about the player's behavior
segments.text:
Adam: Emma, our NPC correspondent, is somewhere in a castle. Emma?
Emma: I guard a doorway. The player is jumping on my head.
Nicole: How long has this been happening?
Emma: Long enough that I have stopped counting. I cannot move. I am scenery.
Adam: To be fair, the jump physics there are incredible.
Nicole: Not helping. Emma, we are sending music instead.

segments.flavor: a real-life situation described entirely in game mechanics, landing a genuine punchline
segments.text:
Adam: A haircut is the character creation screen, except the sliders move while you sit still.
Nicole: And there is no preview. You describe the build out loud and hope.
Adam: Then the mirror comes up. That is the confirm screen.
Nicole: And everyone says yes. Everyone. Nobody has ever said no.
Adam: Because there is no back button. You live in that build for a month.
Nicole: Six weeks. Then the world patches it out and you are new again.
Adam: Ha! New build, new music. Here we go.

segments.flavor: Nicole's lore corner: an absurd 'fact' declared canon with total confidence
segments.text:
Nicole: Canon check. Fire escapes were designed by a level designer who lost a bet.
Adam: What was the bet?
Nicole: That nobody would notice the ladder stops two floors above the ground.
Adam: Wait. Wait. That is a platforming gap. Somebody put a platforming gap on a building.
Nicole: Every one of them. The designer is still laughing somewhere.
Adam: I will never look at a building the same way again.
Nicole: Good. That is what lore corner is for. Take us to the music.

segments.flavor: Emma reports from inside a game as an NPC with feelings about the player's behavior
segments.text:
Adam: Emma is standing in a village square with an exclamation mark. Emma, go ahead.
Emma: My quest has been in the log for three hundred hours. I am still waiting.
Nicole: What is the quest?
Emma: Ten rat tails. It is a bad quest. I know it is a bad quest.
Adam: The reward is the problem. Nobody routes a side quest for twelve gold.
Emma: I would raise it, but the sign is carved in stone.
Nicole: [gentle] Stay hopeful, Emma. Somebody will need those tails one day.
Adam: Until then, music.

segments.flavor: Emma reports from inside a game as an NPC with feelings about the player's behavior
segments.text:
Nicole: Emma is at a finish line somewhere. Emma, how is the race?
Emma: I won. I win every time. The player restarts before I cross.
Adam: Oh, that is a reset. That is just a reset, Emma.
Emma: I have crossed that line four thousand times and never once celebrated.
Nicole: You are allowed to celebrate. Nobody is stopping you.
Emma: [surprised] Oh. Then I am celebrating. Quietly. In the car.
Adam: Ha! Go, Emma. Somebody give her a victory lap track.

segments.flavor: a real-life situation described entirely in game mechanics, landing a genuine punchline
segments.text:
Adam: The self-checkout machine is a boss fight and most people go in with no strategy.
Nicole: It has a phase change. Everyone forgets the phase change.
Adam: Phase one is scanning. Easy. You feel great. You feel fast.
Nicole: Phase two is the bagging area. It speaks. It accuses.
Adam: Unexpected item. That is the boss shouting your own mistake back at you.
Nicole: And then the light on the pole turns on. Help is coming.
Adam: That is a summon. The machine summoned an employee. That is phase three.
Nicole: The employee taps twice and leaves. Nobody knows what they tapped.
Adam: Two taps. Boss defeated. No damage taken.
Nicole: Load the next area. The music is already playing.

segments.flavor: Nicole's lore corner: an absurd 'fact' declared canon with total confidence
segments.text:
Nicole: Time for lore corner, and this one is load bearing.
Adam: Load bearing lore. Go.
Nicole: Every hotel hallway is the same hallway. It is reused to save memory.
Adam: No waaay.
Nicole: Count the doors sometime. The numbers change and nothing else does.
Adam: I am never sleeping in a hotel again. This is a horror fact.
Nicole: The carpet pattern is there so your eyes cannot measure the length.
Adam: That is why the walk to the room takes nine minutes.
Nicole: It is a corridor on a loop. The door number tells the engine to stop.
Adam: And the ice machine is the checkpoint.
Nicole: The ice machine is absolutely the checkpoint. Canon.
Adam: Every hallway, one song. Hit it.

segments.flavor: Emma reports from inside a game as an NPC with feelings about the player's behavior
segments.text:
Adam: Our NPC correspondent Emma is in a village with a hammer. Emma, report.
Emma: I am the blacksmith. I make swords. Nobody buys the swords.
Nicole: What do they do instead?
Emma: They smash my pots. Every visitor smashes every pot in my shop.
Adam: Because pots drop coins. That is efficient. That is optimal routing.
Nicole: Adam. Those are her pots. She made those pots.
Adam: I am sorry about the pots. I would still smash them.
Emma: I refill them overnight. I have accepted this. It is my loop.
Nicole: [gentle] That is the healthiest thing anyone has said on this station.
Adam: Buy a sword sometime, people. Here is a song for the blacksmith.

segments.flavor: back-announce {STREAM} like a high score entry; Adam rates the run
segments.text:
Adam: That was a run. Initials on the board, and I am rating it out loud.
Nicole: He rates every set. He has a scale nobody else can see.
Adam: The scale is simple. Opening, movement, ending, and one point for nerve.
Nicole: Nerve is not a category.
Adam: Nerve is the whole category. That last track started on a drum fill.
Nicole: It did. It walked in like it owned the building.
Adam: Whoever queued that has taste and a spine.
Adam: S rank. No hesitation. Gold split on the chorus.
Nicole: And the bass line at the end?
Adam: Ohhh, that was optimal. Put it in the book.
Nicole: Board is full. Clear it and start the next one.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: The Continue Coin. One heavy brass token, carried in your pocket, for the moment you want to quit.
Nicole: You hold it. You feel it. You keep going.
Adam: The Continue Coin does not fit any machine ever made. That is not the point.
Nicole: Not legal tender, not a real coin, not returnable, and it will set off the airport gate.
Adam: Insert coin to continue. Music continues too.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: Respawn Roast. A dark roast for the morning you did not survive.
Nicole: One cup and you wake up at the last place you felt fine.
Adam: Full health. Half your inventory. That is the trade.
Nicole: Respawn Roast does not restore lost items, lost hours, or anything you said before coffee.
Adam: Brew it hot, sit down, and let this next one play.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: Frame Perfect Shoelaces. The only lace with a one frame tie window.
Nicole: Miss it and the knot fails. Hit it and the knot holds for a lifetime.
Adam: I have hit it twice. Twice! The feeling never leaves you.
Nicole: Frame Perfect Shoelaces come untied for most people. Practice is sold separately and does not help.
Adam: Tie them tight. Track time.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: Inventory Pants. Forty slots, stackable, and one pocket that holds a full sized lamp.
Nicole: The lamp pocket is real. We have seen the lamp.
Adam: Carry your whole life at walking speed. No encumbrance. No penalty.
Nicole: Encumbrance applies after eleven items. Walking speed drops. Sitting becomes a two person job.
Adam: Pack light. Or do not. Here is the next song.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: Hitbox Furniture builds a coffee table with a hitbox smaller than the table.
Nicole: Walk straight through the corner. Your shin stays untouched.
Adam: Every dark room in your home becomes a safe room.
Nicole: Hitbox Furniture cannot hold cups, plates, books, or weight of any kind.
Adam: It is a table in spirit. That counts. Play it.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: The Cutscene Skipper. One button, worn on the wrist, for a story with no end.
Nicole: Press once to summarize. Press twice to nod politely forever.
Adam: Your uncle's dream. The full recap of a movie you already saw.
Nicole: The Cutscene Skipper does nothing. The button is not connected to anything.
Adam: Ha! Press it anyway. It helps. Next track, rolling.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: The Hard Mode Alarm Clock. No snooze button. It has an attack pattern.
Nicole: Learn the pattern, and it lets you sleep eight more minutes.
Adam: Fail the pattern and it moves across the room. It is fast.
Nicole: Nobody has learned the pattern. The clock adapts, and it remembers your name.
Adam: Set it and get up. Wake up music, right now.

segments.flavor: a product only Arcade would sell, sincere announcer grammar, fast disclaimer from Nicole
segments.text:
Adam: Grind Gum. Chew one piece and every boring chore gives experience points.
Nicole: Folding laundry becomes a grind spot. The dishes become a farming route.
Adam: Level up in your own kitchen. Hear the chime. Feel the progress.
Nicole: The chime is in the gum. There are no levels, and the flavor lasts ninety seconds.
Adam: Ninety good seconds. Back to the soundtrack.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: patch notes for real life
segments.text:
Adam: Patch notes for the human body, version whatever we are on now.
Nicole: Knees have been nerfed. Knees were too strong for too long.
Adam: Sneezing now has a wind up animation. You cannot cancel it.
Nicole: Hiccups remain in the game. The team knows. The team is not fixing it.
Adam: Buff to the nap. Naps now scale with how much you needed one.
Nicole: And the itch on your back stays unreachable. Working as intended.
Adam: Working as intended. Ha! Patch notes over, music on.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: achievement unlocked, with rarity
segments.text:
Nicole: Achievement unlocked. You said the right name on the first try.
Adam: Rarity?
Nicole: Point four percent of players have this one.
Adam: Point four! That is rarer than a no hit boss run.
Nicole: Next achievement. You opened a jar on the first attempt, with witnesses.
Adam: Witnesses are required. Without witnesses it does not count.
Nicole: That is why the jar sits on the counter for two days.
Adam: Waiting for an audience. Beautiful. Play us out.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: cheat code corner
segments.text:
Adam: Cheat code corner. Up, up, down, down, and then you say it out loud.
Nicole: Say what out loud?
Adam: The thing you have been avoiding. That is the code.
Nicole: What does it unlock?
Adam: Thirty extra lives. Well, it feels like thirty extra lives.
Nicole: [gentle] That is the best code we have run here.
Adam: Enter it soon. Code accepted. Bring the music up.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: boss music watch
segments.text:
Nicole: Boss music watch. Some moments deserve boss music and never get it.
Adam: Example one. The last stair in the dark, when you think there is one more.
Nicole: Full orchestra. Choir. A low horn that means the floor lied to you.
Adam: Example two. Pulling a sticker off in one clean piece.
Nicole: That is a victory theme, not boss music. Learn the difference.
Adam: Fair. Fair! Example three. Reversing out of a narrow space with people watching.
Nicole: Boss music. Phase two if someone waves you back.
Adam: Correct. Speaking of themes, here is one.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: inventory check and encumbrance
segments.text:
Adam: Inventory check. Empty your pockets and we will read the weight.
Nicole: Keys. Three of them, and one opens nothing anyone remembers.
Adam: Never drop that key. That key is a quest item.
Nicole: One receipt, folded. One coin of a currency you cannot spend here.
Adam: Junk. Sell it to a merchant.
Nicole: You will need it in nine hours and feel terrible.
Adam: That is the real rule. Never sell anything, ever.
Nicole: Pockets full, hands free. Let the next track in.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: the save point survey
segments.text:
Nicole: Save point survey. Every home has one and most people never notice it.
Adam: Mine is the kitchen doorway. I stop there. I do not know why.
Nicole: Because it is a save point. You stand in it and nothing bad happens.
Adam: Ohhh. The light is different there too.
Nicole: Warm light. A quiet hum. That is the save point sound.
Adam: And you always stand in it holding nothing, doing nothing.
Nicole: Saving. That is what saving looks like.
Adam: Ha! Go stand in yours. We will keep the music going.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: loading screen tips
segments.text:
Adam: Loading screen tip. Tip number one. Press any button to continue.
Nicole: That is not a tip. That is an instruction.
Adam: Tip two. Water is wet, and enemies are dangerous.
Nicole: The tips get worse as the load gets longer. That is the rule.
Adam: Tip three. If your health is low, try having more health.
Nicole: There it is. That is a long load.
Adam: Tip four. You are doing fine. Keep going.
Nicole: [gentle] Leave that one in. Load complete, music up.

segments.flavor: the recurring bit: item description of the hour
segments.text:
Nicole: Item description of the hour. A mug, chipped, half full of cold tea.
Adam: Stats?
Nicole: No stats. Flavor text only. It reads, someone loved this once.
Adam: Oof. That is a lot for a mug.
Nicole: Next item. A sock, single, found behind a radiator.
Adam: Sell value, one coin. Sentimental value, unmeasurable.
Nicole: The description says, its partner is out there.
Adam: [sad] Why is the sock sad? Why did you do that?
Nicole: Every good item is a little sad. Next song, please.
